scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: A jar of honey takes the work of thousands of bees visiting millions of flowers. How do bees turn flowers into honey?

scenes.name: nectar
scenes.text: Worker bees sip sugary nectar from flowers and store it in a special honey stomach.

scenes.name: enzymes
scenes.text: Inside the bee, enzymes start breaking the nectar's sugar into simpler sugars.

scenes.name: pass
scenes.text: Back at the hive, the nectar is passed from bee to bee, adding more enzymes each time.

scenes.name: dry
scenes.text: Bees spread it in wax cells and fan their wings to evaporate water, until it's thick honey.

scenes.name: cap
scenes.text: When it's ready, they seal each cell with a wax cap, storing food for the colony.

scenes.name: lasts
scenes.text: Honey is so low in water and slightly acidic, that most germs can't grow in it, so it keeps for a very long time.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Collect, add enzymes, dry, seal. Follow for more on how things really work.
